fix_round_disclosure: Supersedes the first version, which claimed child-usage.mjs 'is user-level tooling per AGENTS.md' and 'not present', citing that .claude/workflows/ is untracked in this worktree. That is true for this worktree (base origin/main 41d39b3) but false as a general claim: the script is tracked project tooling in the agent-lab repository at .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs (commits 549515a, df6effb, reachable from the parent checkout's codex/native-expansion branch, not yet merged to the commit this worktree is based on), and this repo's own AGENTS.md documents invoking it as project-level tooling ('node .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs --latest'), not as an external user-global tool. The prior receipt's evidence_class (local_integration) was also inconsistent with its own commands, which only inspected files/git history (source_review). The fix round compared child-usage.mjs against ccusage on a second workflow run. Reconciliation: that comparison is not the gap's next_check, which needs a retried child and an independent raw-JSONL recompute; see reconciliation.

preregistration.expectation: Run `node .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs --latest` from the agent-lab checkout (read-only; it only reads transcript files) against whatever workflow run this host's Claude Code session directory has most recently recorded, then run `ccusage claude session --json` and look for a session entry keyed by that run's id, then compare the two independently computed sets of the 4 token counters (input/output/cache_read/cache_creation) per resolved model. Given the prior receipt's finding of an exact match on one workflow (wf_76e829b6-778), the informative outcome here is whether a SECOND, different real workflow also matches exactly, or whether the prior exact match was run-specific.
preregistration.criteria: If all 4 counters match exactly for the new workflow too, this further supports (but still does not fully settle, since ccusage still exposes no per-child/per-attempt breakdown) the combined-attribution half of the gap. If any counter diverges, that is new evidence that the prior single-workflow exact match does not generalize, which must be reported honestly rather than smoothed over.

results.live_snapshot_confound: wf_f4b0c001-b52 was still running when both tools read it. In snapshot a its lastActivity is 2026-09-23T01:56:13.034Z, 3 s before the file was written. In snapshot b (02:02:06Z) its sonnet counters had grown to input 1868, output 650399, cache_creation 1819114, cache_read 102978148 (lastActivity 02:02:02Z), while opus was unchanged. The journal grew from 27 lines at review time to 37 lines, last written at 02:23:55Z. child-usage.mjs was run first and ccusage second, and every sonnet difference is ccusage-larger, which is what growth between the two reads produces. The sonnet 'mismatch' is therefore not evidence of a ccusage attribution error.
